| **R1: REL** | **12** | 0 | 0 | 12 |
| **R1: PARTIAL** | 1 | **5** | 2 | 8 |

## Supplementary Table S2 — Per-class Metrics

| Category | TP | FP | FN | TN | Precision | Recall (Sensitivity) | Specificity | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REL | 12 | 4 | 0 | 19 | 0.750 | **1.000** | 0.826 | 0.857 |
| PARTIAL | 5 | 0 | 3 | 27 | **1.000** | 0.625 | **1.000** | 0.769 |
| IRR | 12 | 2 | 3 | 18 | 0.857 | 0.800 | 0.900 | 0.828 |
| **Macro average** | | | | | 0.869 | 0.808 | 0.909 | **0.818** |
| **Weighted average** (by support) | | | | | | | | **0.824** |

**Interpretation:** REL category has perfect recall (no false negatives — every truly relevant decision was identified by both raters); PARTIAL category has perfect precision (when assigned, always correct) but lower recall (some PARTIAL decisions were classified as REL or IRR); IRR shows balanced performance.

## Supplementary Table S3 — Reliability Coefficients

| Coefficient | Value | 95% CI / Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Observed agreement (po) | 0.829 | 29/35 |
| Chance agreement (pe) | 0.361 | Marginal-product expectation |
| **Cohen κ (unweighted)** | **0.732** | 95% bootstrap CI 0.523–0.909 (B=2000) |
| Linear-weighted κ | 0.736 | Disagreements weighted by category distance |
| Quadratic-weighted κ | 0.738 | Larger penalty for distant disagreements |
| Krippendorff α (nominal) | 0.733 | Alternative reliability metric, robust to small samples |

**Landis & Koch (1977) interpretation:** All four coefficients fall in the **"substantial agreement"** band (0.61–0.80).

## Supplementary Section S2 — Sample Size Justification

**Method:** Sim & Wright (2005) normal approximation for κ confidence interval.

**Formula (single-iteration):**
SE(κ) ≈ √[ p₀(1−p₀) / (N · (1−pₑ)²) ]
N_required ≈ p₀(1−p₀) / [ (CI_width / 2 / z)² · (1−pₑ)² ]

**Inputs:**
- p₀ = 0.829 (observed agreement)
- pₑ = 0.361 (observed chance agreement)
- target CI width = ±0.10 around κ
- z = 1.96 (95% confidence)

**Result:**
- N_required ≈ **134 decisions** for ±0.10 CI precision
- N_actual = 35
- Current bootstrap CI width ≈ 0.39 (0.523–0.909)

**Interpretation:** The reported pilot κ value (0.732) is statistically substantive but the wide CI reflects the small pilot sample. For definitive validation a planned prospective cohort of n ≥ 134 is justified (Section 10.1).

**Reference:**
Sim J, Wright CC. The kappa statistic in reliability studies: use, interpretation, and sample size requirements. *Phys Ther.* 2005;85(3):257–268. doi:10.1093/ptj/85.3.257

## Supplementary Section S3 — Disagreement Analysis (n=6)

| No | R1 (expert) | R2 (GPT-4o) | Court type | Likely cause of disagreement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | IRR | REL | Yargıtay 3.CD | Side-reference to "gebe sanık" misread by LLM as obstetric-relevant |
| 5 | IRR | REL | Yargıtay 3.CD (darbe) | Boilerplate "kanunsuz emir" + isolated pregnancy mention |
| 9 | IRR | REL | Yargıtay 3.CD (darbe) | Same pattern as no. 5 |
| 14 | PARTIAL | REL | Yargıtay 2.HD (boşanma) | "Düşük yaptım" claim — LLM upgraded to REL |
| 22 | PARTIAL | IRR | Danıştay | Procedural pregnancy ref — LLM downgraded to IRR |
| 30 | PARTIAL | IRR | AYM | Constitutional context — boundary case |

**Pattern:** All six disagreements concentrate at category boundaries (REL↔PARTIAL or IRR↔PARTIAL). No catastrophic REL↔IRR misclassifications that would affect medico-legal triage at the binary "relevant vs not" decision level.
